It carries execution_kind 'none' and outcome 'blocked' with the specific unblock condition that applies to that measure, so the link asserts that an execution record exists and honestly reports that nothing was run. It is not evidence that the measure passed.

record_verbatim.objective: Compute whether the reference project's configured measurement period meets the acquisition-rate criterion of FB2-SYS-SYR-000001, and record the arithmetic rather than an observation. The criterion is at least 20 acquisitions per second in every monitoring mode; the parameter registry records the acquisition period as 50 ms (FB2-PRM-000003); 1/0.050 s is 20 per second exactly, so the criterion is met with zero margin at the configured value and fails for any period longer than 50 ms. The measure exists because the criterion's figure is a modelled parameter and not a figure any code or measurement in this corpus establishes, which is a different kind of claim from the integrity criterion and needs a different oracle.

oracle_detail.residual_risk: The whole verdict turns on one authored parameter. If the reference project's real period were 55 ms, the criterion would fail and every conclusion downstream of the rate would change.
oracle_detail.what_it_still_does_not_prove: It does not prove that the reference project can achieve that period. Meeting a rate needs the task to be schedulable at that period and the acquisition to complete within it, and neither is established here. It also says nothing about jitter, which a zero-margin rate makes relevant: at exactly the threshold there is no allowance for a late cycle.
oracle_detail.what_the_oracle_is_not: It is not a measured reference: no measurement cycle was counted. It is not source_grounded: the 50 ms figure is a registry parameter, not something read out of the pinned source's code. It is not a synthetic assumption in the sense of an assumed behaviour: the assumption is about a configuration value, and it is recorded as a parameter rather than asserted as a fact about code.
oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: The oracle is the arithmetic of the requirement itself. FB2-SYS-SYR-000001 asks for at least 20 acquisitions per second; the reference project records a 50 ms acquisition period; 1000/50 is 20. No item needs to run for the comparison to have a verdict, and the verdict is sensitive to exactly one input, which is what makes recording that input the substantive part of the measure.

preconditions: The parameter registry entry for the acquisition period is the authoritative configured value for the reference project.
The measurement is a computation over that value, not a run.
record_verbatim.regression_selection: Re-run whenever the acquisition-period parameter changes, whenever the AFE-triggering task's cycle time changes, and whenever the requirement's rate threshold changes. Also re-run on any change that alters acquisition cost, because a rate that was achievable at the current cost may not remain so.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: Authored because FB2-SYS-SYR-000001 had no verification. Split from FB2-VER-TMS-000021 because the rate criterion has a different oracle kind from the integrity criterion, and master prompt section 11 requires that a source-grounded oracle, an analytical model, a synthetic assumption and a measured reference be distinguishable. Merging them would have let a passing integrity check imply a passing rate check.

steps.action: Read the configured acquisition period from the parameter registry.
steps.expected: A single period value is obtained, in milliseconds.

steps.action: Read the configured task cycle time for the task that triggers the measurement from the pinned source.
steps.expected: A single task cycle value is obtained, in milliseconds.

steps.action: Compute the acquisitions per second implied by each value as 1000 divided by the period.
steps.expected: Two rates are produced and compared with each other.

steps.action: Compare the smaller rate against the requirement's threshold and record the margin.
steps.expected: The comparison and the margin are recorded, including that the margin is zero at the registry value.

steps.action: Compute the longest period that would still satisfy the criterion.
steps.expected: A single boundary period is recorded, being the period at which the rate equals exactly the threshold.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
